bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: The two quadrilaterals have equal area
bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
$A$ and $E$ are symmetric about the diagonal $NS$ of the hexagon, so $[SAN]=[SEN]$, hence $[SAND]=[SAN]+[SND]=[SEN]+[SND]=[SEND]$. The sum is $2[SAND]$ and $[SAND]=[SANO]+[DNO]+[DOS]$. Here $[DNO]=\frac12$ (half the unit square), $[SANO]=\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}$ (half the hexagon, since $NA$ is a long diagonal), and $[DOS]=\frac12\cdot1\cdot1\cdot\sin150^\circ=\frac14$ (as $\angle DOS=360^\circ-120^\circ-90^\circ=150^\circ$).

So $[SAND]=\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}+\frac12+\frac14$ and the requested sum is $2\left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}+\frac34\right)=\frac{3+3\sqrt3}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3+3\sqrt3}{2}$**

bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Find the limit point on a side
bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
All three points $A_n,B_n,C_n$ move the same way around the triangle, so $A_nB_nC_n$ stays equilateral and in the limit $A_n$ tends to a point on side $A_0B_0$ at fraction $r$ of its length from $A_0$. Tracking the signed steps along $A_0B_0$: $r=1-\frac12-\frac14+\frac18+\frac1{16}-\frac1{32}-\frac1{64}+\cdots=\frac25$.

The limiting triangle is the inscribed triangle with vertices at fractions $r$ along the sides, whose area is $1-3r(1-r)=1-3\cdot\frac25\cdot\frac35=\frac7{25}$. (A numerical iteration of the midpoint recursion also converges to $\frac{7}{25}=0.28$.)

**Answer: $\frac{7}{25}$**

bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Isosceles triangle $ADE$
bmt-2021-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
$DE\perp BC$ and $AB\perp BC$ give $DE\parallel AB$, so $\angle ADE=\angle BAD=\angle DAE$ and $\triangle ADE$ is isosceles: $AE=DE=x$. Let $\theta=\angle BAC$. Then $\angle ABE=90^\circ-\theta$, so $\angle EBD=\theta$. In right triangle $ABE$: $BE=AB\sin\theta=\sin\theta$ and $AE=AB\cos\theta=\cos\theta=x$. In triangle $BED$, with $DE\perp BD$: $BE=\frac{DE}{\sin\theta}=\frac{x}{\sin\theta}$. So $\sin\theta=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$, i.e. $\sin^2\theta=\cos\theta$, giving $\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-1=0$ and $\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$. Then $AC=\frac{AB}{\cos\theta}=\frac{2}{\sqrt5-1}=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$**
